thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1845679999 - high OOM rate on runtime-serve-prod-4 (gpua-8). paging @oncall_alex

oncall_alex: ack, joining. switching to this channel. quick summary pls

sre_maya: seeing a sustained burst of OOMs on runtime-serve-prod-4 starting ~10:04 UTC. customer errors (502/timeouts) for some endpoints, spike in gpu fragmentation_metric and failed allocs.

ml_infra_raj: attaching pointers to the most recent traces and memory dumps: https://internal/redwood/logs/1845679999 and s3://redwood-internal/oom/1845679999/traces.tar.gz

runtime_dev_liz: i'm digging into allocator traces. initial hypothesis: KV cache growth + high variance in batch sizes leading to fragmentation under load. will try evict + reduce batch cap as live mitigations.

support_jordan: impacted customers: acme-corp (production), beta cohort. error pct observed ~3.2% across affected services. account team notified.

pm_ana: please flag SLA risk and customer comms cadence.

sre_maya: SLA note: risk threshold is 5% sustained errors over 15m. currently ~3.2% and trending down after mitigation kicks in.

oncall_alex: mitigation plan (live):
1) reduce max_batch_size 32 -> 16 on node-group prod-4
2) run targeted KV cache eviction for longest-lived sessions
3) divert a fraction of new traffic to prod-6 to relieve pressure

runtime_dev_liz: applying batch cap now:
```bash
# reduce batch size on group prod-4
redwoodctl set --node-group prod-4 --max-batch 16
```

deploy-bot: config change applied to prod-4; rollout id c3f2. see deploy/1845679999-1

ml_infra_raj: running eviction script (evict oldest 10% of KV entries)
```python
# evict oldest 10% of KV entries
client.kv.evict(percent=10)
```
eviction completed on prod-4 at ~10:12 UTC

sre_maya: quick telemetry after changes: OOM 1m rolling count dropped from ~18 -> 4 within ~3m. avg free GPU memory increased by ~1.8GB on affected GPUs.

runtime_dev_liz: also reduced per-request prefetched context window to 512 tokens for a canary subset which reduced per-request KV growth.

support_jordan: customer comms: ACME updated at 10:22 UTC; they acknowledged mitigation and asked for postmortem.

oncall_alex: started traffic diversion to prod-6 at 10:15 UTC. traffic-router reports ~22% of new requests diverted.

ml_infra_raj: logs excerpt (from prod-4 around the spike):
```
[10:10:04] runtime-serve-prod-4 gpu0: alloc failed: 0x7ff... size=312MB
[10:10:05] kv_cache: entries=1234567 total_bytes=18.9GB
[10:10:06] fragmentation_metric=0.84
```

runtime_dev_liz: hypothesis checklist (live):
- H1: KV cache leak/growth causing high fragmentation — plausible (kv size high, eviction reduced OOMs) ✅
- H2: allocator fragmentation due to varied batch sizes and large allocations — plausible (batch cap improved stability) ✅
- H3: model weight dup/mapping bug causing duplicated buffers — unlikely (no dmesg/driver evidence) ❌

sre_maya: RCA next steps: gather full GPU memory histograms, per-request KV usage traces, and scheduler logs. assignments:
- raj -> histograms + kv traces
- liz -> kernel allocator logs and debugkmem output
- alex -> customer timeline & handoff note

oncall_alex: handoff prep: night oncall @sre_nico in ~2h. compiling timeline for handoff:
- 10:04 incident detected (OOM spike)
- 10:06 oncall page sent
- 10:10 mitigation plan drafted
- 10:12 eviction script executed
- 10:15 traffic diversion started
- 10:17 error rate decreasing
- 10:30 monitoring shows stable error rate near baseline

runtime_dev_liz: allocator debug snippet:
```
kmem: GPU0 free_regions: [0x2000-0x3fff,0x5000-0xafff,...]
coalesced=false
largest_free=1.2GB
```

ml_infra_raj: full traces uploaded to s3://redwood-internal/oom/1845679999/traces.tar.gz (contains per-request kv profiles, gpu histograms, scheduler logs)

support_jordan: confirming ACME postmortem request. they'll want a table of affected windows and estimated request counts.

pm_ana: please include customer impact table (requests affected, time windows, mitigation timeline) in the final RCA doc.

sre_maya: quick root-cause note: likely composite failure: unchecked KV cache growth combined with high allocation variance produced allocator fragmentation under heavy load. mitigations that worked: forced eviction, batch cap, and traffic diversion. follow-ups: add automatic eviction thresholds, workload-aware batch tuning, and alerting on fragmentation_metric thresholds.

oncall_alex: closing incident channel for now — filing formal incident ticket linking logs and this thread. handing off to @sre_nico for PM/postmortem follow-up. thanks all :thumbsup:

sre_nico: ack, i'll pick this up for the postmortem. pls attach any remaining logs before 12:30 UTC.
